messages:
Oliver (CS): Noticed a cluster of onboarding sign-ins failing with 401s for EU tenant batch starting ~02:20 UTC. I pulled an impacted list (7 trials, 3 enterprise) and dropping it here so eng + legal can advise on comms. Link: https://go/internal/cs/impacted-auth-mig (view).
Tasha (eng-oncall): Thanks. Early signals show a recent config rollout toggled `enable_token_cache=false` in eu-1 during a staged deploy. That caused cache misses and immediate token expirations to be treated as invalid by our token validator. Rolling back the latest FLAG config for eu-1 now.
infra-bot: config-rollout: rollback initiated for eu-1 (run-id c-roll-2026-09-28-0225)
Ken (Product): Which customers are impacted? Any in active renewal discussions? We should prioritize outreach if so.
Oliver (CS): Impacted enterprise: GreenField (onboarding, renewal review in 6 weeks), MarketLoop (pilot), and 3 smaller trials flagged. GreenField flagged as high renewal risk.
Bri (CS Ops): Recommend: immediate targeted note to impacted contacts, offer a complimentary onboarding session for enterprise, and 14-day credit for trials. I can prepare personalized invites. Also suggest scheduling follow-up to capture voice-of-customer feedback to the renewal tracker.
Lina (Legal): Credits ok. Quick guidance: avoid admitting fault language. Use neutral phrasing and "we apologize for the inconvenience". Prefer phrasing like "authentication flows returned to expected behavior for affected users as of <time>".
infra-bot: config-rollout: rollback completed for eu-1 (run-id c-roll-2026-09-28-0225) - success
Tasha (eng-oncall): Rollback finished at 02:35 UTC. Authentication flows returned to expected behavior for affected users by ~02:38 UTC. Root cause: accidental flag flip during a config promotion step. Immediate fix: restore flag. Follow-up remediation: add pre-promote validation for critical auth flags, canary the next rollout to 1 host per region, and alert on auth error spike (owners: infra team). Postmortem scheduled for 10:00 UTC.
Oliver (CS): Drafting the customer note below. Please review (Legal especially) before we send.
Oliver (CS): --- CUSTOMER NOTE DRAFT ---
Hi <CustomerName>,
We want to make you aware of a brief issue that affected some sign-ins during onboarding earlier today. A configuration change caused certain EU-based logins to be rejected; authentication flows returned to expected behavior for affected users as of 02:38 UTC. If you are still seeing 401s, please try a fresh browser sign-in and include the request timestamp and the x-rw-trace header when you get back to us so we can investigate immediately.
We apologize for the inconvenience. As a goodwill gesture, we've applied a 14-day credit to affected trials and scheduled a complimentary 1:1 onboarding session for impacted enterprise customers. If you'd like hands-on troubleshooting, book here: https://cal.link/redwood-cs/office-hours.
If you have any questions, reply to this thread or contact your CS rep directly.
---
Lina (Legal): Approved with minor change: replace "we've applied" with "we have applied" for tone, and keep the phrase "we apologize for the inconvenience". Also change "we want to make you aware" to "we're writing about". Otherwise good.
Oliver (CS): Updated per Legal. Will send to the impacted list at 03:00 UTC and post a short portal notice. Bri, please DM me after you finish calls so I can annotate renewal risk updates.
Bri (CS Ops): Will do. I'll log all call notes and any churn indicators in the renewal tracker and capture feedback in the customer feedback sheet.
Tasha (eng-oncall): Monitoring shows auth error rate back to baseline by ~02:42 UTC. Postmortem will include timeline, the config audit diff, and remediation tasks (pre-promote checks + canary + alerting). I'll add runbook steps for quick rollback to prevent recurrence.
Oliver (CS): Sent the customer notes at 03:02 UTC. I'll update this thread with any reply that looks like an executive escalation or renewal risk.
